subject: Human Evolution
title: Long-Distance Trade
description: Learn Long-Distance Trade in one minute.

hook.text: A Mediterranean shell turns up 800 km inland at an ice age camp. Somebody moved it—or traded for it.

buildup.text: During the Upper Paleolithic, raw materials and ornaments traveled vast distances across Europe.

discovery.text: Trade networks connected distant groups, spreading materials, ideas, and cultural practices.

twist.text: Networks provided insurance: when local food failed, distant allies could offer refuge or supplies.

climax.text: Ice age trade wasn't just commerce—it was a social safety net woven across a harsh continent.

punchline.text: Survival depended on friends you'd never met.

quiz.question: What role did trade networks play during the ice age?
options: Spread materials, ideas, and provided social safety nets
